title: NHSBSA Baby Loss Certificate (BLC) Live Service

content.text: From: DHSCAssessment date: 25/06/2026Stage: Live assessmentResult: Green Service provider: NHS Business Service Authority (BSA)
Service description

The Request a Baby Loss Certificate service was born out of the Pregnancy Loss Review. Currently, there is no formal recognition of baby losses prior to 24 weeks gestation, leaving some bereaved parents struggling to find closure. DHSC commissioned NHSBSA to create the service to fill this gap. It is an online application form which, upon successful completion, results in a physical certificate of loss. The aim is to provide recognition of a life lost and to provide comfort to bereaved parents. It is an optional service, and it is not a legal document.
Service users
This service is for...
Anyone who has a parental relationship to a baby which was lost before 24 weeks of pregnancy who lives in England and their baby loss was in England.

10. Define what success looks like and publish performance data
Decision
The service was rated green for point 10 of the Standard.

The existing KPIs are useful, but they do not provide a sufficiently strong view of user outcomes, journey friction, service quality or improvement priorities. We should retain operational SLA measures but introduce a more decision-focused KPI framework that demonstrates whether the service is delivering timely and accurate recognition to bereaved parents, where users are encountering difficulties, and where investment or service improvements should be targeted.

11. Choose the right tools and technology
Decision
The service was rated green for point 11 of the Standard.
The team has consciously chosen technologies that fit the problem rather than over-engineering the solution.

The team demonstrated that its technology choices are aligned to the service's needs and operating model. The architecture makes effective use of managed cloud services and a decoupled design. The use of SQS to separate user-facing journeys from downstream fulfilment processes provides an appropriate buffer against failures or delays in dependent services and supports efficient event-driven processing.

13. Use and contribute to open standards, common components and patterns
Decision
The service was rated green for point 13 of the Standard.

The team demonstrated appropriate use of open standards, common components and established patterns. Technology decisions prioritised reuse of proven capabilities over bespoke implementation, helping to reduce delivery risk and ongoing support overhead.

14. Operate a reliable service
Decision
The service was rated green for point 14 of the Standard.

The team demonstrated a pragmatic and proportionate approach to service reliability. Resilience considerations have been built into the architecture through the use of multi-AZ deployment, clearly defined recovery objectives, monitoring and alerting, operational runbooks and a decoupled design that reduces dependency on downstream systems. The approach appears appropriately aligned to the service's criticality and operational needs, avoiding unnecessary complexity whilst maintaining an appropriate level of resilience.
